These individuals, once prominent, have faced significant setbacks, sometimes due to personal misconduct, public scandals, or poor decision-making.

His wife also filed for divorce during his time in office.

Chris Christie, the former Governor of New Jersey, faced a dramatic fall from grace after the Bridgegate scandal, in which his allies created a traffic jam to target a Democratic mayor. His low approval ratings and controversial actions, including being seen on a state beach during a government shutdown, further damaged his reputation.

James Comey, the former FBI Director, became a polarizing figure during the 2016 presidential election. His public criticism of Hillary Clinton and the timing of his announcement about an FBI investigation contributed to Donald Trump’s victory. Trump later fired Comey, citing conflicting justifications.

Mark Fields, the former CEO of Ford Motor Company, was let go in 2017 despite a rise in corporate revenue. His tenure was marked by a significant drop in stock prices and a failed strategy to compete with Tesla through investments in electric and autonomous vehicles.

Tiger Woods, once the top-ranked golfer in the world, has faced a series of personal and professional scandals, including infidelity and a recent DUI incident. His ranking has plummeted to 899, the lowest in his career, following a publicized incident involving prescription drug use.

These stories illustrate the fragility of power and fame, showing how quickly individuals can fall from grace in the public eye, regardless of their previous status or achievements.
